**Finding: missing — insurance covenant absent (severity: low).**

The agreement contains no insurance provision anywhere: a full-text search for "insurance" returns zero hits, and neither the indemnity (Section 12) nor the miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13–30) impose any coverage obligation on TrueLink. Because TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data, this falls into the rule's walk-away category (no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data). The gap is compounded by TrueLink's liability cap at 12 months' hosting/support fees (p0077), which leaves its Section 12(b) indemnity effectively unbacked.

Redline validated (ok:true): new **Section 31 (INSURANCE)** inserted after Section 30 (Force Majeure) at the preferred level — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, maintained through the term plus one year. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if that better matches TrueLink's existing program.

One drafting note for the negotiation, not flagged as a separate issue: Section 24 (p0090) recites that "Sections 1 and 5 through 30" survive; if the new Section 31 is accepted, that survival list should be conformed to reference Section 31 so the one-year tail coverage obligation survives termination.
